summary: The study investigates the electrical and optical properties of TiO2 thin films prepared by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) on Si(100) and glass substrates. The films were annealed in the temperature range of 500–900 8C, leading to the formation of crystalline TiO2 in the anatase phase. The dielectric constant improved significantly after annealing, reaching up to 75 at 100 kHz for films annealed at 700 8C. However, the leakage current increased with annealing temperature due to the formation of oxygen vacancies and grain boundaries. The study also highlights the importance of annealing in optimizing the dielectric properties of TiO2 films for electronic applications.
evidence: We report on the electrical and optical characterisation of the high-permittivity (high- k) TiO2 thin films grown by plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition on Si (100) and glass substrates, respectively. TiO2 films were incorporated in metal-oxide semiconductor (MOS) capacitor structures with an Al metal gate electrode. The as-deposited films were amorphous; however upon annealing in the temperature range 500 – 900 8C, crystalline TiO2 in the anatase phase was formed. The dielectric constants were calculated from capacitance – voltage (C– V) curves of the MOS structure on the as-deposited film and annealed films revealing a significant improvement of the dielectric constants from 10 to 75 at AC frequencies of 100 kHz for the 700 8C annealed TiO2 thin films. The increase in the dielectric constant for annealed films could be attributed to the transformation of film structure from amorphous to polycrystalline (anatase). However, the transformation of amorphous to crystalline phase, leads to an increase in the leakage current which was also found best fitted with Schottky emission mechanism at moderated electric fields.
